same_scenario_mapping.reason: Path A request/runner, joined report, token review, status board, and Path B UI report carry the same Row12 scenario identifiers.

layer_verdicts.reason: All required nested outputs were located and parsed from Path A core response.
The request became a universal task with task_id, task_title, task_type, constraints, deliverables, acceptance_gates, raw_prompt_redacted=true, raw_prompt_sha256, and explicit non-claims.
task_type is plan_only_or_approval_gated_task, which matches the synthetic request to produce a bounded Smart Skills execution plan without external AI.
The task became a universal orchestration plan with exactly 3 ordered steps; each step has uses and one verification_gate.
Selected skills are exactly the allowed route set and no unapproved skill was found.

The core response labels candidate-order and candidate-position material as diagnostics/scaffold only and says selection authority is blocked; it does not use order or position as final semantic authority.
Path A and supporting review packets keep forbidden claims false: token savings, semantic quality, readiness, training, checkpoint mutation/promotion, locator update, and external AI.
Path B correlates to the same scenario/pair/marker/hash and shows the Cursor UI route, but submitted_to_core=false, so it is route correlation only.

Row12 identifiers are preserved through request correlation, runner mapping, task_id, raw prompt hash, joined report, token review, and Path B report. The core response's nested CheckSetResults.references object itself reports marker, scenario_id, and pair_id as not-provided.

Evidence is sufficient for this narrow structural Row12 eval, but it is baseline/partial for semantic quality: no held-out/source-disjoint set, no before/after quality comparison, no ablation, no no-memorization proof, and no regression guard.
Token counts, screenshots, status rows, and joined readiness evidence were used only for mapping/boundaries, not as semantic quality proof.
